text: For integers a and b (a ≠ 0), the statement 'a divides b' (written a ∣ b) means:
choices: a < b and a shares a digit with b
there exists an integer k such that b = a·k
b divided by a leaves a remainder equal to a
explanation: By definition a ∣ b holds iff there is an integer k with b = a·k. Option A ('a / b is an integer') actually expresses b ∣ a — the opposite direction. Option D misdescribes division, since a ∣ b corresponds to remainder 0, not remainder a.
